slides.title: 风险与分歧

bullets.text: To summarize in a sentence: I think language complexity is a big problem, but I think GATs themselves are a great addition…
This isn't an argument against implementing GATs, but there are some concerns I have about both syntax and some... non-obvious uses
I'm also concerned with forcing significant changes too quickly: I see a lot of NLL and scoped thread breakage…
But this tendency to only do so in the narrow window between FPC and the next release is concerning and problematic

notes: To summarize in a sentence: I think language complexity is a big problem, but I think GATs themselves are a great addition, but I think their interaction with WF is a leaky abstraction that needs to be plugged.
This isn't an argument against implementing GATs, but there are some concerns I have about both syntax and some... non-obvious uses.
I'm also concerned with forcing significant changes too quickly: I see a lot of NLL and scoped thread breakage and soundness issues in the queue right now, for example.
But this tendency to only do so in the narrow window between FPC and the next release is concerning and problematic.

slides.title: 结论与决策

bullets.text: The "Review of what is proposed for stabilization" seems better to read before "Major options"
I'd rather these issues be resolved before pushing the feature into stable, not after
I am in favor of keeping up the momentum to fix the problems and get these features stabilized
(link) Agree with @skyzh, without GAT it's really hard for us to write vectorized expressions in simple way
